node.statement: For fixed finite n, h_n is the matrix amplification: for Z=[Z_ij], h_n(Z)=[h(Z_ij)] on the Hilbert direct sum (S_{P,Q},q)^n. Thus ||h_n(Z)|| <= (sum_{i,j}||h(Z_ij)||^2)^(1/2) <= K_1*(sum_{i,j}||Z_ij||^2)^(1/2) <= n*K_1*||Z||; the last inequality uses contractivity of matrix-coordinate compressions in the registered operator-space structure, so ||Z_ij||<=||Z||. Therefore h_n is a bounded linear map and b_n=||h_n||<=n*K_1<infinity even when S_P is infinite-dimensional. Finally, for T=h_n(Z), the operator C*-identity gives ||T||^2=||T^dagger*T||, and lem-hcb2-amplified-adjointness gives T^dagger=h_n(Z^dagger). This proves exactly the usable conclusion of node 1.2.1 without its erroneous finite-dimensional premise.
